transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

I keep getting stuck redoing the same checks and routines over and over at work, even when I know they’re unnecessary. It's really starting to derail my projects and my life, and I just can't seem to stop.
Do you also get unwanted, intrusive thoughts or fears that drive you to do these checks and routines, even though you know they’re excessive?

Yes, I get these looping thoughts that if I miss a tiny detail, like a mislabeled bolt size or a minor tolerance error, something catastrophic will happen and people will get hurt. Even though I know it's completely irrational, I just can't block those vivid images of parts failing out of my head. It feels impossible to stop them.
Do these thoughts and checking rituals feel hard to resist because they reduce your anxiety, and do you recognize that they are excessive or unreasonable even while you feel driven to do them?

Yes, absolutely—the logical part of my brain knows that checking a file for the tenth time is completely excessive and unnecessary. But the anxiety and fear of a catastrophic failure are so overwhelming that I feel this uncontrollable drive to do it just to get a moment of relief. It’s incredibly frustrating to feel so ruled by something I know makes no sense.
How long have these unwanted thoughts and checking rituals been happening, and do they take up more than an hour a day?

They started about a year ago during a major product rollout at work while I was also studying for my PE exam. They definitely take up way more than an hour a day; I can easily lose an entire hour just rechecking a single CAD file or email. It's gotten to the point where I'm staying at the office past midnight and skipping my workouts just to finish these routines.
Do you ever try to resist the checking or avoid situations that trigger it, and if so, what happens to your anxiety or functioning when you try to stop?

I find it incredibly difficult to resist or stop once I get started because it feels completely out of my control. I'm not really sure how to describe what happens when I try to fight it, other than it feeling nearly impossible to do.
When you try to resist the checking or skip a routine, do you feel a surge of anxiety or distress that only eases after you do the ritual?

Yes, absolutely. If I try to walk away, my anxiety spikes massively and I get overwhelmed by those thoughts of parts failing and people getting hurt. Performing the check is the only way to temporarily quiet that persistent feeling that I've missed something, which is why I feel so chained to these routines.
Do you also have any other repetitive behaviors or mental rituals, like washing, counting, ordering, repeating words, or checking things outside of work?

No, I don't really experience those kinds of rituals like washing, counting, or ordering. My repetitive behaviors are almost entirely focused on checking and re-checking my work-related designs and emails.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has clear obsessive-compulsive symptoms with recurrent intrusive catastrophic thoughts, compulsive checking rituals, recognition that the behaviors are excessive/unreasonable, marked anxiety relief after rituals, time-consuming symptoms (>1 hour/day), and significant functional impairment. The presentation is most consistent with obsessive-compulsive disorder.
